label: Today You Will Learn
h: How to separate what a person actually said from what you imagined, prepare only your own part, and go in intending to hear.
body:
About 8 minutes, plus one short pause · one small practice · no homework list

If the person you are rehearsing for has been abusive, coercive or unsafe, do not use this lesson to prepare contact. Seek specialist advice first; the wise decision may be no conversation at all.

label: Key Scripture
h: "If one gives an answer before he hears, it is his folly and shame."

label: Name The Pattern · Rehearsal
body:
The confrontationThey grow more unreasonable; you grow more eloquent.
The defenceAn answer to the criticism, then to the follow-up, then the next.
The explanationAn apology polished for the perfect wording that never arrives.

label: The Main Truth
h: Rehearsal supplies evidence that does not exist, and makes you arrive already in the middle.
body: Most often, it replaces the conversation altogether.

label: Three Things That Look Alike
body:
PreparationYour facts, your purpose, your opening words. Has an end. Leaves you ready to listen.
Bounded planningA few realistic responses, held as possibilities. Responsible for hard conversations.
RehearsalScripts the other person. Treats the script as evidence. Never ends.

label: A Common Belief
h: "If I do not rehearse, I will be caught out."
body: Your responsibility is faithfulness and clarity, not control of another person's response.

label: The Tool
body:
1. Notice: "I am rehearsing."
  2. What has this person actually said to me about this?
  3. Is a real conversation needed? Choose a time and a method.
  4. Prepare only my part: two or three opening sentences.
  5. Go in intending to hear.

label: Do This Now
h: Take the conversation you have been rehearsing most. Write only what the other person has actually said, and when.
body:
Then one line: Everything after that was mine. Or: They have said more than one thing, and a conversation is needed.

Pause the audio

label: Remember
h: My part is prepared. Their part is not mine to write.

label: Prayer
body:
Father, you know the conversations
I have been holding alone.

Give me words for my part,
and ears for theirs.

The outcome is yours.

Amen.
